summary: Teotihuacan has you moving worker dice around a modular board, where each die's pip value grows every time you use it, letting you unlock better and better actions over the game. Much of the tension comes from timing when to reset a maxed-out die versus riding it for one more powerful action, all while racing to contribute to the shared central pyramid.
praised: the die-growth engine is elegant and satisfying to optimize
tightly interlocking systems that reward planning
strong solo mode and scaling across player counts
criticised: heavy analysis paralysis from the branching action choices
steep learning curve similar to other heavy worker-placement games

interaction.detail: Worker-dice move around one common modular board of location tiles, and each location offers only one of two areas at a time, so occupying a tile can deny its action or bonus to other players that round. Resources and technology tiles sit on shared board spaces to be claimed, though each player builds their own separate temple/warehouse structures with what they gather.

scoring.how_you_win: You build up the most VP across pyramid contributions, technologies, god worship, and completed goals by the time the pyramid is finished or the era track runs out.
